text:
maria: heads-up — since the canary yesterday we've seen p99 regressions for short-sequence requests (~45ms increase) and KV hit-rate drops on the same hosts. suspect the continuous batcher is letting long sequences dominate batches and is causing KV churn. attaching profiling notes in-thread.
leo: ugh. which model / kernel combo on the canary? flash-attn or older kernel?
anika: canary used v2.1 runtime with auto-kernel-selection enabled (flash-attn preferred). payload mix: 70% short (<64 tokens) interactive requests, 20% medium, 10% long (>512).
maria: exact profile summary pasted below:
```
host: gpu-12
model: redwood-english-3b
kernel: flash-attn (fallback: cuBLAS custom)
p50: +2ms
p95: +8ms
p99: +45ms
throughput: -7% (steady 5m window)
kv_hit_rate: 0.68 -> 0.56
batch_size_mean: 12 -> 18
long_seq_share_in_batches: 0.34 -> 0.61
```
dave: KV hit rate drop is scary. are long sequences evicting prefix cache entries? our KV admission policy is LRU per-GPU.
sophia: likely. with larger batches dominated by long sequences we hold more KV cache per request and evict entries for popular short tenants. symptom fits tenant-starvation.
leo: do we have tracing that correlates tenant id -> KV eviction events? maybe tenant hotness skew.
anika: yes, traced a sample. short-tenant A had 15x more cold starts; eviction traces show repeated KV rehydration for same prefixes.
maria: interestingly, kernel selection logs show flash-attn was chosen ~92% of the time but fallback to slower kernel didn't spike; so not purely kernel perf, it's batch composition + KV pressure.
dave: propose quick mitigation: 1) add per-tenant KV reservation buckets (small with fast expiry) for short-tenants, 2) cap long-sequence contribution to continuous batches (token-budget target), 3) enforce mini-batch preemption for short requests.
leo: +1 to token-budget targeting. current algorithm uses token-credit per-lane: {
```
lane_short: target_tokens=512
lane_long: target_tokens=4096
credit_refill_ms=20
```
} which lets long lanes accumulate and then hog.
sanika (typo) -> anika: can we try aggressive smoothing: lower long target to 2048 and increase short target to 1024 for the canary group?
sophia: Also consider KV pin for top-5 short tenants on those GPUs during peak windows.
maria: ops-bot, can we roll a canary with these config changes to 3 hosts? small window (30m) and collect eviction traces + per-tenant p99.
ops-bot: received. creating canary job with config: {
  "batching": {"token_budget":{"short":1024,"long":2048}, "preemption":true},
  "kv": {"tenant_pin_top_k":5}
}
deploy-bot: canary scheduled to hosts gpu-12,gpu-17,gpu-19. rollout start in 5m.
leo: while canary runs, I can add a lightweight queue policy metric: fraction_of_batches_with_long_share>0.5 and kv_eviction_rate.
danika -> anika: typo — ack.
dave: longer term we should alter continuous-batcher: when forming a batch, prefer filling first with short requests up to X tokens, then append long requests. effectively bounded headroom for long sequences.
sophia: agree. also we should add kernel-routing hint: if batch has mixed seq lengths, prefer kernel path tuned for small sequences to avoid per-token slowdowns for short items.
leo: that might require per-batch kernel decision rather than per-model. doable but needs careful cost model; I'll prototype an estimator using sequence-length-weighted kernel latency.
maria: agreed. immediate plan: run the ops canary, collect per-tenant p99, kv hit-rate, batch composition. if improvement > 20% on p99 for short-tenants and kv_hit_rate recovers, promote config. if not, rollback and try harsher preemption.
anika: i can prepare dashboards: short-tenant p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, batch_mean_size, long_share_in_batches.
dave: action items assigned: leo -> kernel-routing estimator prototype (2d). anika -> dashboard + eviction traces. maria -> monitor canary and convene post-canary sync. sophia -> prepare KV pinning script. ops-bot -> canary rollout.
maria: thanks all. quick note: add a short blameless note for product teams — some short interactive customers may get flaky latencies briefly.
leo: ping me if you want extra tracing knobs (tenant tags, sample rate).
ops-bot: canary finished: collecting metrics (ETA 28m).
